q_45367.question_text: What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q2 FY2027 earnings release? (Revenue)
q_45367.reasoning:
Let me work through this systematically.

## (a) Time left until resolution
The question asks about NVIDIA's forward guidance (not actual results) to be released on August 26, 2026. Today is August 25, 2026. Resolution occurs in approximately **1 day**.

## (b) Most likely outcome and why

The question asks specifically about **forward guidance** for Q2 FY2027 revenue, which NVIDIA will issue during their earnings call on August 26, 2026.

Key facts from the research:
- NVIDIA already issued guidance in May 2026 for Q2 FY2027: **$91.0 billion ± 2%** (range: $89.2B–$92.8B)
- Wall Street consensus: ~$91.9 billion
- Jefferies (outlier): forecasts actual Q2 results of $95 billion and **guides for Q3 FY2027 of $108 billion**

The critical insight: NVIDIA typically provides forward guidance one quarter ahead. During the Q1 FY2027 earnings call (in May), they already provided guidance for Q2 FY2027 ($91.0B ± 2%). During the Q2 FY2027 earnings call (tomorrow, August 26), they will issue guidance for **Q3 FY2027**.

The question asks for "forward guidance" in the Q2 FY2027 earnings release. The natural interpretation is the guidance they provide at that call—which would be for Q3 FY2027, not Q2 FY2027.

Jefferies specifically forecasts Q3 FY2027 guidance at **$108 billion**, significantly above the current $104 billion consensus. The range provided (99.5B–115.5B) is much wider than typical historical ±2% guidance, suggesting it's intended to capture possible Q3 FY2027 guidance scenarios.

## (c) What would push the value lower?

- Conservative execution: If actual Q2 results come in weak or in line with the lower end of prior guidance ($89.2B), management might be more cautious with Q3 guidance
- Macro concerns: Slowing demand signals, inventory adjustments, or geopolitical uncertainty could warrant more modest forward guidance
- Market saturation: If data center demand appears to be plateauing
- Conservative guidance pattern: NVIDIA typically provides achievable guidance to manage expectations

## (d) What would push the value higher?

- Strong Q2 results: If actual revenue significantly beats the $91B guidance (approaching Jefferies' $95B forecast), confidence in higher Q3 guidance increases
- Demand momentum: Sustained AI/data center strength, with customers pulling in orders
- Supply chain confidence: Ability to ramp production to meet demand
- Bullish management tone: Jefferies' $108B Q3 forecast suggests material upside to consensus is possible and credible
- China dynamics: Any positive developments on China export restrictions could enable higher guidance

## (e) Base rate or historical reference values

The research provides:
- Prior guidance (May 2026 for Q2): $91.0B ± 2% 
- Wall Street consensus for Q3: $104B
- Jefferies outlier: $108B

NVIDIA's typical guidance pattern shows ±2% precision, but forward-looking guidance for a growth company can vary more widely. The provided range (99.5B–115.5B) is approximately ±8% around a ~107.5B midpoint, which is wider than typical ±2% but reasonable for a full quarter ahead with execution and demand uncertainty.

## Reasoning on the distribution

Given:
1. The range focuses on Q3 FY2027 guidance (most likely interpretation)
2. Wall Street consensus: $104B
3. Jefferies bullish case: $108B
4. The range spans 99.5B–115.5B
5. NVIDIA has a pattern of conservative-but-achievable guidance

The median should be slightly above consensus (~$105-106B), reflecting that:
- Jefferies' $108B is a thoughtful outlier from a credible analyst, not pure speculation
- Management typically guides conservatively but within the realm of credibility
- Strong AI momentum and demand support higher guidance vs. 2024-2025 norms

For the 10th/90th percentiles, I'd expect tails to reflect realistic scenarios where Q2 beats big (pushing Q3 guidance higher toward $110-112B) or disappoints (pulling guidance down toward $101-103B).

q_45367.research_text:
NVIDIA is scheduled to release its Q2 FY2027 earnings on Wednesday, August 26, after market close [morningstar.com](https://www.morningstar.com/stocks/going-into-earnings-is-nvidia-stock-buy-sell-or-fairly-valued-8). For Q2 FY2027, NVIDIA's own guidance, issued in May, projected revenue of $91.0 billion, plus or minus 2%, implying a range of $89.2 billion to $92.8 billion [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/) [cnbc.com](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/05/20/nvidia-nvda-earnings-report-q1-2027.html). This guidance assumed no data center compute revenue from China [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/) [cnbc.com](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/05/20/nvidia-nvda-earnings-report-q1-2027.html).

Wall Street analysts, according to Yahoo! Finance, have an average revenue estimate near $91.9 billion [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/). Jefferies, however, forecasts NVIDIA will report Q2 FY2027 revenue of $95 billion, and guide for Q3 FY2027 revenue of $108 billion, significantly above the $104 billion consensus [finance.yahoo.com](https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/articles/1-veteran-analyst-sees-nvidia-115749161.html). This would represent NVIDIA's largest-ever quarterly revenue beat [finance.yahoo.com](https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/articles/1-veteran-analyst-sees-nvidia-115749161.html).
